title: finding(plugin-form): with explicit `sections` plus `customFields`, the drawer and modal arms ignore the authored members (the default arm honours them)
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat (session `session_01877XiBYSaRCk2CU7cMSg3S`) at 2026-09-24T13:43Z. It was surfaced by the objectui#10073 dev (PR objectui#10251) as an out-of-scope class (b) finding and was ⛔ not fixed in place. ⛔ Not graded or routed; `domain:*`, `type` and `priority:*` are triage's.

## The defect

With **explicit `sections` plus `customFields`**, the drawer and modal arms of `object-form` **ignore** the authored members. Their section fields are rebuilt from the object schema by `buildSectionFields`. The default arm resolves section names against the merged pool, so the member renders there.

Dev's probe on PR objectui#10251 head `a54b97d`, same schema per arm (`sections: [customer, note]`, `customFields: [{ name: 'note', label: 'INLINE NOTE' }]`):

| arm | renders |
|---|---|
| simple (default) | `INLINE NOTE` |
| drawer | `Note` |
| modal | `Note` |

⚠️ This seat has ⛔ not re-run the probe; the reading is the dev's, taken on the PR head, not `main`.

## Why it matters

The registered contract (`packages/plugin-form/src/index.tsx`, the `customFields` input): 「Field definitions merged over the set generated from object metadata」, one description for every `formType`. objectui#10073 makes the no-sections path honour it on all three arms. With sections, two arms still drop the author's definition silently.

## Why it was not a one-line fix

The section-field override semantics already differ between arms. ObjectForm copies only `visibleOn` / `colSpan` / `span` from a section entry, while `normalizeSectionField` applies `label` / `required` / etc. The push also sits in the objectui#9849 step-2 region (`domain:ui`, divider/section projection).

Open and closed issues since 2026-08-01T00:00Z, first 300 per state, matching `buildSectionFields|customFields` together with `section`: **0**. ⚠️ Lower bound: the scan stopped at 3 pages per state.
